text:
tara: FYI: acme-inc called in — they report a sudden p99 spike and intermittent 502s starting ~2026-03-15T18:02:00Z. customer says p95/jitter is fine most of the day, sudden degradation at ~18:00. ticket #3421 attached. I captured one failing curl they used:

curl -i -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate -H 'Authorization: Bearer <token>' -d '{"input":"hello"}'

They hit 502 / timeout after ~10s; other requests succeed. Can someone triage? :warning:

javier: on it. which tenant and region? any quick telemetry?

tara: tenant: acme-inc (prod-us-west). They reported ~200 RPS at peak; normally ~25 RPS. We throttled some, but alerting started when p99 > 5s. logs: "upstream response timeout" and a bunch of queued requests.

lindsey: grabbing telemetry now — checking ingress queues, admission metrics, and worker pod CPU.

ops-bot: Incident alert: p99_latency(prod-us-west, model: redwood-13b) crossed 5s threshold at 2026-03-15T18:03:12Z. queue_depth=312; active_workers=6; worker_cpu_p95=94%

sam: quick note — model-serving pool had concurrency limit of 12 per pod and HPA target was 6 pods; autoscaler didn't scale because CPU window didn't trigger (requests spend time waiting in queue not pushing CPU immediately). looks like admission control kept accepting until queue hit hard limit.

javier: this matches a classic admission + burst load combo. two immediate mitigation options: 1) temporarily raise replicas / force scale to drain queue; 2) reduce admission (shed) to keep latencies under SLO by rejecting some requests; or 3) fallback to a cheaper model variant for bursts. which do we want first?

tara: customer prefers no rejects if possible — they asked for faster recovery. can we scale first?

sam: doing a forced scale now. kubectl command: ```
kubectl scale deployment/model-serving-redwood-13b -n prod --replicas=12
```

deploy-bot: rollout started: deployment/model-serving-redwood-13b scaled from 6 -> 12 replicas by sam at 2026-03-15T18:06:03Z

lindsey: watching backlog. queue_depth -> 312 -> 120 -> 38 in the last 2m. p99 dropped from ~6.2s to ~1.2s after first 3 replicas came up.

javier: good. we should still consider admission changes so a future spike doesn't refill queue faster than autoscale. suggestion: lower concurrency-per-pod to 8 and enable request_shed at 95th percentile for the next 30m. that will make each pod handle fewer concurrent requests and let autoscaler see CPU signal earlier.

sam: patching concurrency: ```
kubectl patch deployment/model-serving-redwood-13b -n prod --type='json' -p='[{"op":"replace","path":"/spec/template/spec/containers/0/env/CONCURRENCY","value":"8"}]'
```

ops-bot: config-change noted by sam at 2026-03-15T18:09:20Z.

lindsey: added temporary admission policy change (30m): shed_rate_threshold=95 -> start dropping 10% of requests above threshold. applied at 18:10.

javier: also enabled fallback route for acme-inc to model redwood-7b for generation requests if model-serving-13b queue > 200. that reduces tail latency while preserving successful responses. routing change: ```
PATCH /v1/routing/policies/acme-inc
{ "fallback_model": "redwood-7b", "trigger_queue_depth": 200 }
```

tara: I've informed acme support contact: "We're scaling the pool and enabling temporary fallbacks; you should see p99 improvement in minutes. We'll follow up once we finish root cause analysis."

(2 minutes later)

lindsey: update: queue_depth stabilized < 40, worker_cpu_p95 dropped to 64%, p99 ~ 820ms, no new 502s observed in logs.

javier: good containment. we should treat this as a regression candidate for autoscaler/metrics — autoscaler didn't react because requests were queued and not driving CPU. action items: 1) improve autoscaler to consider queue_depth and request_latency as scaling signals; 2) add a short-circuit metric that increments when admission queue > X to force scale; 3) postmortem if same pattern repeats.

sam: filing infra issue for autoscaler change, will include simple sim to reproduce queue-driven stalls.

deploy-bot: note: manual scale rolled back to HPA-managed after 35m at 2026-03-15T18:41:00Z — replicas returned to baseline 6.

javier: follow-up for support: please ask customer to share any traffic shape (sudden fan-out?) and if they used any orchestrated load generator. also ask if they saw concurrent retries — retries can amplify bursts.

tara: will request and attach to ticket #3421. also suggested they enable client-side jittered backoff for retries.

lindsey: post-containment checklist posted to #incidents for next rota. I'll own the short postmortem if we see reproduction steps.

javier: thanks all. temporary mitigations: manual scale, concurrency tuning, fallback route, admission shed. Outcome: p99 returned to acceptable range and 502s stopped. We'll keep the thread open for customer-provided repro and autoscaler follow-up. :white_check_mark:
